bullets.title: Mike Wallace Is Here
bullets.note: ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07VK1GBM5/ref=pv_ag_gcf?cmp=rt_where_to_watch), [Apple TV](https://itunes.apple.com/us/movie/mike-wallace-is-here/id1473541702?cmp=rt_where_to_watch), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LtWdKJP106w)). This doc found me at exactly the right time. I was in the midst of studying many different types of interviewers ([Terry Gross](https://freshairarchive.org/guests) vs. [Larry King](https://www.cnn.com/specials/app-style-section/larry-king-interviews) vs. [Joe Rogan](https://open.spotify.com/show/4rOoJ6Egrf8K2IrywzwOMk) vs. [Charlie Rose](https://charlierose.com/) vs. [James Lipton](https://www.bravotv.com/inside-the-actors-studio/videos), etc.) to improve my own game. Mike is an archetype of the Southern Tiger Claw kung fu style of interviewing, kicks to the balls included. He can be brutal. And while I wouldn’t duplicate all aspects of his approach, I think there is much to learn. Some of the clips in this doc are tense beyond words. The footage of Mike with Ayatollah Khomeini, as one example, will make your stomach do flips. Here’s the official description: “For over half a century, _60 Minutes_’ fearsome newsman Mike Wallace went head-to-head with the world’s most influential figures. Relying exclusively on archival footage, the film interrogates the interrogator, tracking Mike’s storied career and troubled personal life while unpacking how broadcast journalism evolved to today’s precarious tipping point.” You can [find the trailer here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dDSq2fF9flk). Highly recommended.

bullets.title: “MDMA is the reason my son has a father instead of a folded flag.”— US Army SGT (R) Jon Lubecky (@jonlubecky) This quote is at the end of a recent, short video from The Today Show led by Savannah Guthrie (@savannahguthrie): “New research shows how psychedelic drug can help people with PTSD.” To learn more, read “Veterans Have Become Unlikely Lobbyists in Push to Legalize Psychedelic Drugs,” which was published at nearly the same time in The New York Times_. People on the right and left don’t agree on much, but this is one area where we can find common ground with good data. Take a look at these odd bedfellows. Also, be sure to see the P.P.S. at the end of this email.
bullets.creator: US Army SGT
